name: roofs_house_a
prompt:
Two images are attached. The first is a layout: 16 building outlines seen from above, in a 4×4 grid on a flat magenta background. The second is finished art from the same game, to match in style only — not its layout, shapes, colours or the size of its details.

Make one image with exactly the same 4×4 layout as the first image. Inside each outline, draw the roof of the building described for that cell below, as a top-down sprite for a 2D city game.

Shape comes first. Before painting a cell, trace its outline exactly, then paint only inside the traced border:
- Keep every outline's proportions: match each one's width and height. Some are long thin strips almost three times wider than deep, some nearly square, three deeper than wide. Never make an outline squarer, shorter or fatter. Each cell's proportion is given below; check it.
- Every edge is straight and square to the others. Never slant, skew or taper an edge to show perspective.
- Draw nothing outside the outline, not even eaves, steps, canopies or shadows. Inside a roof there is no magenta at all.

Scale is the second rule, and it is strict. Every size below is true metres, width × depth, and every detail is drawn at its true size against them. These are small buildings next to cars four metres long: a 5 m roof is only a little longer than a car.
- A brick chimney is about 0.6 × 0.6 m: a small square, about a ninth of the depth of a 5 m roof.
- A roof tile course or a corrugation is about 0.2–0.3 m: fine, closely spaced lines, twenty or more across a 5 m roof, never a few broad stripes.
- A skylight or roof window is about 0.8 × 1 m. A gutter is a thin line along the eave.
- A lean-to porch on the street side is about 1.5–2 m deep and covers only part of the front.
- No detail is bigger than its true size. When in doubt, draw it smaller and keep fewer of them.

Rules for every cell:
- Look straight down (orthographic). No perspective, no walls seen from the side, no tilt, no ground, no plants, no shadow cast outside the roof.
- The thick bottom edge of each outline is the street front, where the entrance is. The top edge is the back.
- A gabled roof shows its ridge as one line along the long axis with the two slopes shaded differently; a lean-to roof is one slope falling to one edge, with no ridge in the middle.
- Style: match the style image. Clean, flat-shaded cartoon game art, bold dark outlines, muted natural colours, simple readable details, soft light from the top-left.
- Outside the roofs, keep the background flat pure magenta #FF00FF. No text, numbers, labels, signs, grid lines or frames anywhere.
